newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas softens in summer, OTC focuses on promp.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas softens in summer, OTC focuses on promp.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures were off in the summer on Tuesday morning, with July and August showing some weakness although September ticked up by 0.01 pence a therm in a single trade.

A futures broker was uncertain over whether the announcement by Transco that it is to sell 3 TeraWatt hours (102 million therms) of gas by tender from its balancing margin storage by the end of May was behind this weakness. But he agreed that it is likely to keep prices depressed over the summer.
Futures trade was thin once again, with only 35 lots transacted in four separate deals. August saw the biggest losses, down by 0.050 pence a therm

Most market interest was on physical gas in the prompt period. A power generator which had bought heavily on Monday confirmed that it had also been active on Tuesday morning. A spokesman for the company said that it had bought "in the order of half a million therms" on the within day market at around 10.70 pence a therm, and was also looking at the day ahead market where prices were at around 10.60 to 10.70 pence a therm.
The within-day prices have softened since Monday, when deals were done at up to 11.50 pence, although day-ahead prices are largely unchanged.
